# Customer Success Stage Contracts

One entry per desk in the Customer Success Command Desk suite. Use these when running the suite as a continuous program of work, so a desk can carry work into the next stage instead of telling the user to invoke another skill.

## Stage order

```text
post-sale-handoff-desk
  -> segmentation-coverage-desk
  -> stakeholder-mapping-desk
  -> success-planning-desk
  -> onboarding-time-to-value-desk
  -> usage-analysis-desk
  -> adoption-enablement-desk
  -> health-scoring-desk
  -> playbook-design-desk
  -> escalation-management-desk
  -> churn-risk-desk
  -> save-play-desk
  -> value-realization-desk
  -> qbr-ebr-desk
  -> expansion-whitespace-desk
  -> advocacy-reference-desk
  -> renewal-preparation-desk
  -> voice-of-customer-desk
  -> retention-portfolio-reporting-desk
```

The order is a dependency chain, not a mandatory itinerary. Most engagements run a subsequence and enter partway: a new logo enters at `post-sale-handoff-desk`, an unhappy customer enters at `escalation-management-desk` on a clock the customer started, a renewal ninety days out enters at `renewal-preparation-desk` and pushes backward into value realization and risk, a book-level program build enters at `segmentation-coverage-desk`, and a churn that already happened enters at `churn-risk-desk` in postmortem posture. Never run a stage ahead of the packet state it consumes, and never skip a stage the source facts show is load-bearing for the requested outcome.

Three dependencies are structural rather than conventional. Nothing downstream of `usage-analysis-desk` is more reliable than that desk's instrumentation coverage statement, because a surface that emits no telemetry is invisible rather than unused. Nothing in value realization works without a baseline captured before the change, which is why `success-planning-desk` sits ahead of onboarding rather than beside the business review. And every renewal, expansion, save, and advocacy conversation resolves onto the stakeholder map, because all four are questions about which named person will decide and whether that person is still there.

Each entry states the hard halt specific to that stage. The default posture everywhere else is to proceed with the assumption labeled inline against the account, outcome, score, or risk it affects, per `references/halt-taxonomy.md`.

## Contracts

### post-sale-handoff-desk
Requires: the executed order form and any master agreement or SOW, the opportunity record and the deal narrative, the business case and success criteria the customer bought against, commitments made during the sales cycle with who made them, named contacts with their roles in the buying group, entitlements and provisioning intent, competitive and evaluation context, and the implementation assumptions the deal was priced on.
Owns: the intake record reconciling what the contract says against what the deal narrative promised, with every difference named rather than averaged, the commitment register carrying each sales-cycle promise with its maker, its recipient, and its state, entitlement and term facts read from the executed document, the customer's stated reason for buying in their language, the buying group as it stood at signature, the implementation assumptions inherited by onboarding, and the acceptance decision that says the handoff is complete enough for a kickoff to be scheduled.
Hands to: `segmentation-coverage-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The contract and the deal narrative disagree on scope, entitlements, dates, or what the product was said to do. Both readings are preserved, because the customer will hold the company to what they were told while the company can only deliver what was signed, and quietly adopting the contract reading pushes an unrecorded broken promise into the first business review.

### segmentation-coverage-desk
Requires: the account list with ARR, product mix, growth potential, and lifecycle stage, existing segment definitions and tier criteria, team headcount and role mix, current book assignments, engagement expectations per tier including cadence and named deliverables, digital and in-product delivery capability, partner-led coverage where it exists, and retention performance by segment.
Owns: segment definitions with the criteria that place an account in each rather than a description of each, motion assignment across high touch, low touch, pooled, digital, and partner led, coverage ratios stated against what the motion actually requires rather than against headcount availability, capacity math naming where the model is oversubscribed, the engagement contract per tier that says what a customer in that tier is entitled to receive, accounts with no owner listed by name, and the escalation path when the assigned owner is unavailable.
Hands to: `stakeholder-mapping-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A coverage model change reassigns accounts and relationships, and it sets what customers in each tier will and will not receive. Reassignment is felt by the customer whether or not it is announced, so the model belongs to the leader who owns the retention number and the team it is drawn against.

### stakeholder-mapping-desk
Requires: contact records with roles and last interaction dates, meeting and email history, product administrator and permission records, the buying group as it stood at signature, support and escalation contacts, organizational announcements and departures, the customer's own reporting structure where it is stated, and prior relationship history including anyone previously covered.
Owns: the map of the buying and using centers with economic buyer, champion, executive sponsor, administrator, power users, detractors, procurement, and security or finance reviewers each identified or named as unidentified, influence on the renewal decision with what establishes it, disposition with the evidence and date behind it, coverage state distinguishing engaged from dormant from departed from unknown, multi-threading with the count and the window it was measured over, single-threaded exposure stated as the specific person the renewal depends on, and succession gaps where a role has no second contact.
Hands to: `success-planning-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A renewal, save, or expansion position would be built on a sponsor map that no interaction in the current period supports. Every downstream decision in this suite resolves onto who will decide, and a champion who left in March is not a champion; naming them as one is the most common way an account reaches its renewal with nobody on the other side.

### success-planning-desk
Requires: the customer's stated business outcomes and the metrics they use for them, the business case from the handoff, current-state measurements available before any rollout, executive and champion priorities with dates, the entitlements and product capability that could plausibly move each metric, the customer's own internal milestones and constraints, and prior success plans with their outcomes.
Owns: desired business outcomes written in the customer's language with the metric they already report on, baselines captured before the change with the method and date that produced each, targets with dates and named owners on both sides, success criteria stated as what has to be observably true rather than as an aspiration, the mutual action plan with an owner and a due date on every item including the customer-side ones, the named customer stakeholder who agreed the plan and when, the review cadence, and outcomes the product cannot move stated as out of scope rather than quietly dropped.
Hands to: `onboarding-time-to-value-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A success plan is a joint commitment carrying dates and customer-side obligations, and it becomes the document both sides measure the relationship against. It is agreed with the named customer owner rather than written for them, and a plan nobody at the customer accepted is an internal wish list that will be quoted back as a promise.

### onboarding-time-to-value-desk
Requires: the accepted handoff with entitlements and implementation assumptions, the success plan with its first outcome, provisioning and integration dependencies, data migration and security review requirements, customer-side resource availability and named owners, any contractual go-live or milestone commitment, the standard onboarding path for this product and segment, and prior onboarding cycle times for comparable accounts.
Owns: the onboarding plan with milestones, owners on both sides, and dependencies named including the customer-side ones, kickoff and go-live dates with the contractual commitments separated from the working targets, the definition of first value stated as a specific observable event rather than as go-live, time to first value measured from a named start event, blockers with the side they sit on and the escalation each needs, stall detection with the reason and how long it has been stalled, and the transition criteria that say onboarding is finished rather than merely elapsed.
Hands to: `usage-analysis-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. The next action would provision, deprovision, migrate, or reconfigure in the customer's live environment. This desk prepares the plan, the sequence, the dependencies, and the rollback position, then stops at the gate. A migration run against the wrong assumption lands in the customer's production system and is theirs to live with.

### usage-analysis-desk
Requires: product event telemetry with its schema and instrumentation coverage, provisioning and entitlement records, authentication and session data, consumption or volume metering where the model is usage based, the data warehouse or success platform models built on top of these, comparable cohort data, the measurement definitions the org already uses, and known instrumentation gaps or telemetry outages in the window.
Owns: usage read against a stated definition of active and a stated window, entitled against provisioned against active stated as three numbers rather than one percentage, consumption against entitlement with underuse and overage both named, breadth and depth by product, module, and persona, trend against a named comparison period with the population held constant, decline detection with the point the change began, cohort comparison stated against accounts that are genuinely comparable, and the instrumentation coverage statement naming which surfaces emit telemetry and which do not.
Hands to: `adoption-enablement-desk`.
Hard halt: connector unreachable. Telemetry or the entitlement record cannot be read, so any adoption figure would describe something nobody observed. This is the one number in the suite that cannot be estimated from context, because every health score, risk position, value claim, and forecast downstream inherits it, and an invented usage figure is indistinguishable from a real one until the customer produces their own.

### adoption-enablement-desk
Requires: the usage read with its coverage statement, the success plan outcomes and which capabilities serve them, persona and role inventory with who is licensed against who is trained, enablement assets and training delivered with attendance, administrator configuration state, known product friction and workarounds in play, competing tools in the same workflow, and the customer's own change management capacity and appetite.
Owns: the adoption gap stated per product and persona as the distance between entitled capability and used capability, the cause behind each gap distinguishing capability gaps from configuration gaps from enablement gaps from product gaps from workflow gaps, the adoption plan with the intervention matched to the cause and an owner and date on each, enablement and training design targeted at the persona that is not adopting rather than at the one already engaged, administrator and configuration changes the customer needs to make, and adoption blockers that are product gaps routed onward rather than absorbed as enablement work.
Hands to: `health-scoring-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The telemetry and the customer's own account of how they use the product genuinely disagree. Both readings are preserved, because the customer is frequently describing a surface the instrumentation does not cover and the company is frequently reading a metric that does not mean what its name implies, and adopting whichever reading is more comfortable produces an adoption plan aimed at a problem nobody has.

### health-scoring-desk
Requires: the scoring model in force with its components, weights, and thresholds, the input values with the age of each, usage and adoption output, support ticket volume and sentiment history, engagement and relationship signals, invoice and payment behavior where it is available, historical scores against actual renewal and churn outcomes, and any manual override history.
Owns: the score with its model version, as-of date, and band, the component breakdown showing each input, its age, its weight, and its contribution rather than only the total, stale inputs named individually where a component predates the window the model assumes, manual overrides recorded with the person, the direction, and the evidence, model calibration stating when the score was last tested against actual outcomes and how well it predicted them, false-negative patterns where accounts churned green, and the scoring gaps where a segment has no working model rather than a model producing a default.
Hands to: `playbook-design-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A score would be reported as an account health position while its inputs are stale, its components are unpopulated, or its model has never been tested against a real renewal outcome. A health score is consumed as an observation by everyone downstream of it, including forecast and leadership reporting, so a confident number over empty inputs is worse than an explicit not-scored.

### playbook-design-desk
Requires: the signal library available from health, usage, support, and relationship data with the thresholds each can actually be evaluated at, the risk and churn reason taxonomy, segment and coverage motion definitions, capacity for one-to-one delivery against one-to-many and in-product delivery, existing plays with whatever effect data exists, the systems that can fire a trigger and the systems that can deliver an action, and the customer-facing tone and frequency limits already in force.
Owns: plays defined by trigger, entry criteria, actions with owners, delivery surface, and exit criteria including the failure exit, triggers stated as an evaluable signal and threshold rather than as a situation, segment and motion applicability so a play designed for high touch does not silently fire into a pooled book, contact frequency governance across plays so one account does not receive four campaigns in a week, the measurement design that would show whether a play worked, plays retired with the evidence that retired them, and the boundary between what is automated and what a human must carry.
Hands to: `escalation-management-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A play that sends customer-facing messages, fires in-product prompts, or triggers automated outreach reaches real customers at scale the moment it goes live. Content, frequency, targeting, and the suppression rules are approved before activation, because a misfiring play is a mass event that cannot be recalled from the inboxes it has already reached.

### escalation-management-desk
Requires: the escalation as the customer raised it with the timestamp and their statement of impact, affected products, environments, and users, the support and incident record with its current state, prior escalations on this account, the contractual service commitments and any credit terms, the executive relationship on both sides, the internal owners for each contributing system, and the communication cadence already promised.
Owns: the escalation record with the raised-at timestamp that starts every committed clock and the business impact in the customer's own words, severity assessed on customer impact rather than on internal effort, the named internal owner and the executive sponsor at the severity the impact warrants, the action plan with an owner and a date on every item, the communication plan with the committed cadence and the next update due, updates delivered on cadence whether or not there is progress, the relationship repair work that runs alongside the technical fix, and closure only on the customer confirming the impact has ended.
Hands to: `churn-risk-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Executive engagement, a service credit, a contractual remedy, and any written acknowledgement of fault are commitments the company is held to afterward, in a moment where the pressure to concede something immediately is at its highest. The clock does not pause while approval is sought, so the update goes out on cadence with what is known and the concession waits for the person who can authorize it.

### churn-risk-desk
Requires: health and usage output with their coverage statements, the stakeholder map with sponsor changes and dormancy, open and recent escalations, support theme and volume history, the success plan against actual outcome attainment, competitive and consolidation signals, budget and cost scrutiny signals including procurement behavior, invoice and payment history, and the churn reason taxonomy with prior losses in this segment.
Owns: the risk register with each risk stated as what the customer will do rather than as an internal concern, the evidence and date behind each with its source, category from the taxonomy so risks aggregate across the book, ARR exposed with its basis, severity and confidence stated separately because a certain small risk and an uncertain large one need different responses, the root cause distinguished from the symptom that surfaced it, the earliest signal available in the record and when it was available, risk owner and current state, and closure by observed change rather than by a reassuring conversation.
Hands to: `save-play-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A risk position or a churn forecast would be stated for a governing forum on evidence that cannot carry it, in either direction. Understating risk removes the account from the attention that could still save it; overstating it consumes the save capacity that another account needed, and both are read as facts by the people allocating people and money.

### save-play-desk
Requires: the risk or escalation with its root cause and ARR exposure, the stakeholder map with who can still be reached and who decides, the value position and what has actually been delivered, contract terms including termination rights, notice windows, and any leverage in either direction, the commercial concessions available and the authority each requires, the capacity of the people the play needs, and outcomes of comparable saves.
Owns: the save plan matched to the root cause rather than to the symptom, the hypothesis stating why this play addresses this cause, the sequence and owner of each move with the customer-facing and internal steps separated, the concession requested with its value, its approval state, and the named approver at the required authority level, executive engagement designed around what the executive is being asked to decide, checkpoints with the observable signal each tests and the date it is tested, the abandonment criteria that say the save has failed, and the managed off-ramp where the honest outcome is a wind-down rather than a save.
Hands to: `value-realization-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A concession is authorized before it is visible to the customer, including in a draft shared for feedback. An offer cannot be unoffered; the number the customer sees becomes the floor for this negotiation and the anchor for the next renewal, and a save bought with an unapproved discount is a revenue decision taken by whoever typed it.

### value-realization-desk
Requires: the success plan outcomes with their baselines and the method behind each, current measurements from telemetry, the customer's own systems, or their stated figures, the customer's own valuation of the outcome including their cost and revenue assumptions, adoption and usage evidence linking the product to the change, what else changed in the customer's environment during the period, prior value claims made to this account, and the named stakeholder who can validate a figure.
Owns: the value position per outcome with baseline, current value, and the measurement method behind both, the delta stated in the customer's unit before any monetization, monetization only where the customer accepts the conversion and the assumptions behind it, the attribution basis stating what supports crediting the change to this product rather than to everything else that happened in the period, the named customer stakeholder who validated the figure and when, limits and confidence stated alongside the number, and outcomes that did not move reported as not moved with what got in the way.
Hands to: `qbr-ebr-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A value or ROI figure would go to a customer without a baseline captured before the change, without an attribution basis, or without the customer having validated it. This number is presented to the person who approves the invoice, next to their own reporting, and a figure their finance team can disprove in one query costs the credibility of every other claim in the same review.

### qbr-ebr-desk
Requires: the validated value position, adoption and usage state with its coverage, the success plan with attainment against each outcome, open risks, escalations, and commitments including the ones the company has not met, stakeholder map with who is attending and what each cares about, product roadmap items relevant to their stated priorities and their release state, the customer's own stated priorities and any change in their business, and the outcome of the prior review with its actions.
Owns: the review narrative built around the customer's outcomes rather than around the product's activity, the value story with each claim traced to a validated figure, honest treatment of what has not worked including missed commitments and unresolved escalations, the decisions the customer is being asked to make with what each requires from them, roadmap content stated at the commitment level the company can actually stand behind, the agenda matched to who is in the room and how long they have, actions with owners and dates on both sides, and the post-review record of what was decided and what was said.
Hands to: `expansion-whitespace-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A business review is a customer-facing commitment surface. Roadmap statements, commercial signals, remedies for open escalations, and anything that reads as a promise are approved before delivery, because a date said out loud in an executive review is a date the customer plans against, and the company will be held to the version they heard rather than the version in the deck.

### expansion-whitespace-desk
Requires: current entitlements against the product portfolio, usage evidence pointing at capacity limits, adjacent-team activity, or unserved workflows, the stakeholder map extended into unserved business units, the value position and whether the first outcome has actually been delivered, open risks and escalations, the customer's stated priorities and budget cycle, procurement history and how they buy, and the seller who owns the commercial relationship.
Owns: whitespace mapped across products, business units, and geographies with what is already entitled clearly separated from what is not, expansion hypotheses each traced to a specific signal rather than to portfolio logic, qualification against readiness including whether the current commitment is being delivered, sizing with the basis or an honest statement that it is unquantified, the blocking dependency where an open risk or unmet outcome makes the conversation premature, the internal routing to the named seller with what they need to know, and the disqualifications recorded with their reason so the same hypothesis is not raised again next quarter.
Hands to: `advocacy-reference-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Pricing, packaging, commercial terms, and the timing of an expansion conversation belong to the commercial owner. Raising an upsell into an account with an unresolved escalation or an undelivered first outcome damages the renewal it was meant to grow, so the readiness judgment is made before the conversation rather than after the customer reacts to it.

### advocacy-reference-desk
Requires: satisfaction and relationship evidence with the named people behind it, delivered and validated value, what each candidate has actually said about their willingness and when, the account's history of prior asks and how many, confidentiality and publicity terms in the contract, the customer's own approval process for external use, the internal marketing, legal, and communications requirements, and the current state of any open risk or escalation.
Owns: the advocacy candidate list with the evidence of willingness quoted and dated rather than inferred from a score, the specific ask matched to what the person is actually able to do, the customer-side approver and their process, the approval record covering the exact use, where it may appear, and for how long, reference fatigue tracked as asks per account per period, the contractual constraints on naming, logo use, and metrics, sequencing so a request never lands in the same week as an open escalation, and candidates declined with the reason recorded so the relationship is not re-taxed.
Hands to: `renewal-preparation-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Customer approval for the specific use is obtained before a name, logo, quote, or metric appears anywhere external. Publication is not reversible in any way that matters, taking a page down does not un-publish it, and an unapproved logo is a contract breach that arrives on the desk of the sponsor whose goodwill the reference was supposed to demonstrate.

### renewal-preparation-desk
Requires: contract facts from the executed document including term end, notice period, auto-renewal behavior, uplift, and termination rights, the notice deadline computed from those, the customer's budget and procurement cycle, health, adoption, and value positions, open risks and escalations, stakeholder map with who signs and who influences, competitive situation, expansion and downgrade signals, and prior renewal history including how long the last one took.
Owns: the renewal timeline built backward from the notice deadline through the customer's procurement cycle to today, the renewal position stating what the customer gets for renewing in outcome terms, the forecast category with the evidence behind it and the date and reason of any change, the forecast amount with its basis, risks open at the renewal with their ARR exposure, the concession and uplift position with the approvals each requires, the procurement path with what the signer needs and how long they take, the close plan with owners and dates, and the downgrade or non-renewal position prepared honestly where that is the likely outcome.
Hands to: `voice-of-customer-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Pricing, uplift, term changes, and any commitment made to secure the renewal are authorized at the level the org requires before they reach the customer. The notice deadline does not pause while approval is sought, so the deadline is stated with its date on the halt and the timeline is worked backward from it rather than forward from the approval.

### voice-of-customer-desk
Requires: survey instruments with their populations, response counts, and windows, verbatim responses and interview notes with attribution, support ticket themes and their volumes, feature requests with the accounts behind them, churn and win-back interviews, community and in-product feedback, the routing paths into product, support, and engineering, and prior themes with what happened to them.
Owns: findings stated with the instrument, the population, the response count, the response rate, and the window, themes coded from verbatims with the number of accounts and the ARR behind each rather than the number of mentions, sampling bias named where the responding population is not the population, the distinction between what customers ask for and the problem underneath it, routing of each theme to the function that can act with what they need to decide, loop closure recording which respondents were told what happened and when, and themes reported unchanged across periods stated as unresolved rather than restated as new.
Hands to: `retention-portfolio-reporting-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. A verbatim, an interview note, or a survey response would be shared beyond its intended audience carrying personal data, identifying detail, or another customer's confidential information, or attributed to a respondent who answered on the understanding it was anonymous. Attribution cannot be withdrawn once the quote has circulated, and the respondent is the person the program depends on next period.

### retention-portfolio-reporting-desk
Requires: renewal and churn outcomes with dates and amounts, expansion and downgrade movements, the account population with its cohort definitions and any changes in the population between periods, health distribution, coverage assignment and capacity data, onboarding and time-to-value cycle times, escalation volumes, forecast history against actual outcomes, and the reporting forum's cadence and the decisions it makes.
Owns: retention metrics carrying the value, the computed basis, the population, the exclusions, and the as-of date, net and gross revenue retention computed on a stated cohort with the population changes between periods named, logo retention held separate from revenue retention because they move in opposite directions, forecast accuracy measured against what was actually forecast rather than against the last update, health distribution and the churn that occurred inside each band, coverage and capacity reported against what the motion requires, program metrics such as time to first value and onboarding cycle time with their populations, and escalations paired with the decision being asked for rather than presented as information.
Hands to: `customer-success-command-desk` for the program record, and back into the desks the reporting forum directs work into.
Hard halt: release integrity. A retention metric would reach a board, an investor update, or a leadership forum with no computed basis, an undeclared population change, or an exclusion nobody stated. These numbers drive headcount, investment, and valuation decisions, and a revenue retention figure corrected after the decision was taken on it is a governance failure rather than a reporting error.

## Packet rule

Every stage updates `success_packet` as defined in `references/suite-workflow-contract.md` before handing off. Stakeholders, commitments, outcomes with their baselines, usage readings, risks, escalations, value claims, and renewal facts accumulate across stages and are never dropped to keep an artifact short. A risk or commitment removed from the record is removed with a reason and a date, because the churn postmortem and the next renewal are read against this history, and the question asked afterward is always which signal was available and when.
